text: Oct 12, 2026 In collaboration with scientists and research partners, Google is helping to make disease more detectable, treatable, and preventable — with the goal of improving health outcomes. Yossi Matias VP, Google & GM, Google Research Pushmeet Kohli VP Science, Google DeepMind & Chief Scientist, Google Cloud Your browser does not support the audio element. Google is using artificial intelligence to accelerate medical research, from mapping the human brain to identifying genetic diseases in under eight hours. These tools help scientists repurpose drugs, design custom enzymes, and improve cancer detection rates while reducing administrative burdens on doctors. You can explore these open-access platforms and research findings to see how technology is transforming patient care and public health outcomes globally. Google is using AI to help scientists understand diseases at a tiny, molecular level. These tools speed up drug discovery, map the human brain, and help doctors diagnose patients much faster. The technology also helps predict disease outbreaks so communities can get the care they need sooner. By sharing these tools, Google hopes to help researchers everywhere create better treatments and save more lives. Google’s health research and tools span from fundamental cellular discovery to laboratory analysis and patient impact. Over the last five years, Google teams have published 90 peer-reviewed research papers about understanding and addressing diseases, accumulating more than 90,000 citations. And building on our vision for how technology can accelerate science to improve lives , we’re collaborating with clinicians, academic institutes, and researchers to ensure discoveries make it out of the lab to benefit patients. Here is how our efforts are helping to advance medical research and public health solutions. AlphaGenome Atlas is the most comprehensive catalog of predictions for how single-letter variant changes in the human genome affect molecular biology. To effectively treat an illness, it helps to understand how it operates at the molecular, genetic, and cellular levels. Our early-stage biology models act as collaborative research tools for scientists, revealing nature's hidden mechanics and advancing medical discoveries. Visual map of proteins developed with the support of AlphaFold. The lab is where biological discovery is validated, engineered, and turned into potential medical and public health solutions. Our models have replaced slow, iterative processes with systems that can process large amounts of data quickly and accurately. New mammography screening systems can help to catch historically missed interval cancers and reduce specialist reading workloads. A medical breakthrough only matters if it can help real people. Our research demonstrates that machine learning models can help support disease detection as well as alleviate the administrative workload so providers can focus on care. Transforming health requires scientists, researchers, and institutions working hand-in-hand. That’s why we equip the science community with the advanced models and open-access platforms to fuel breakthrough research — along with the philanthropic funding and computing power they need to apply that research. Through Google.org, we’re supporting organizations like the Infectious Disease Institute at Makerere University to forecast malaria drug resistance mutations with AlphaFold and AlphaMissense, and the University of Pennsylvania, using AlphaProteo and AlphaFold to help design novel cellular therapies that can augment the treatment of solid tumors and complex diseases. In 2026, Google.org has provided over $60 million to organizations around the world that are applying advanced models to transform how we understand and treat diseases. By meeting disease at every stage, we can turn the most intractable human health challenges into actionable solutions, helping people everywhere live longer, healthier lives.
